incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 — unusual auth traffic observed
incident-bot: Detected high-rate 401/403 to idp-proxy from edge-log-relay (svc=logshipper). Possible leaked debug lines referencing internal s3 paths. See telemetry snapshot: https://playbook.internal/alerts/3151599999
samir_oncall: ack, taking this. I’m paged and jumping in. Starting triage now.
leah_sec: on call for sec. Can you paste a minimal log sample and affected tenants? Prioritize customer-facing keys.
matt_prod: I see a blip in the router: sudden 50x auth attempts from a small set of IPs, then a stream of requests to our staging log forwarder. No incidence of model inference errors yet.
jenna_sre: adding context — our log-forwarder was recently updated yesterday to include debug path metadata. If that got shipped to external buckets it could expose path fragments.
samir_oncall: minimal log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T21:12:03Z INFO auth idp-proxy request_id=abc123 status=403 user_agent="logshipper/2.1" path="/staging/customer-42/logs/2026-03-17/debug.txt" hint="s3://redwood-staging-logs/customer-42/2026-03-17/debug.txt"
```
leah_sec: thanks. That path hint is worrying. Need to confirm whether the logshipper sent full payload to external bucket or forwarded to 3rd party. Who owns the log-forwarder creds?
matt_prod: service account is svc-logshipper@redwood-inference. It uses an ephemeral token from our internal token service and an S3 upload role.
leah_sec: immediate mitigation steps: 1) revoke the current upload role session tokens 2) disable log-forwarder outbound connector 3) rotate the staging S3 upload role and repair least-privilege policy 4) assess if any customer PII present.
olivia_cs: heads up — customer-42 is a pilot with two active customers on that tenant. We should prepare a short notification for them if exfil confirmed. No public customers impacted yet that I can see.
samir_oncall: executing quick containment: disabling outbound connector now.
incident-bot: action: connector disable triggered by samir_oncall at 3151599999.7 — command: `infractl connectors disable logshipper-outbound --region=us-east-1`
samir_oncall: connector disabled. Confirmed no further outbound requests from logshipper in the last 60s.
jenna_sre: initiating token revocation for svc-logshipper sessions. Running: `authctl sessions revoke --service=svc-logshipper --reason="suspect-leak-3151599999"`
leah_sec: also request a KMS key rotation for the role that signs upload tokens. I’ll coordinate with infra-keys.
matt_prod: I'll snapshot the forwarder config and pull the audit log for the last 24h to see destination endpoints.
jenna_sre: quick audit sample shows 14 external endpoints in the last hour; 2 of them are unknown hostnames (not in allowlist).
leah_sec: treat unknown endpoints as potential exfil sinks. Initiate bucket ACLs check and preserve objects for forensics, but do not delete. Tag and quarantine suspect objects.
samir_oncall: preserving objects with: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging-logs/customer-42/2026-03-17/debug.txt /forensics/3151599999/ --cli-read-timeout 0` — copied for analysis.
leah_sec: good. Next, rotate the upload role keys and update the forwarder to use short-lived tokens only. After rotate, we’ll run a canary to ensure no customer traffic broken.
matt_prod: can we do a quick impact check on other tenants? Running query: `SELECT count(*) FROM log_forwarder WHERE path LIKE '/staging/%' AND dest NOT IN (allowlist)`
jenna_sre: initial query returns 7 tenants with debug-level uploads in the window; flagging them for audit.
olivia_cs: prepping a customer note template: short summary, what we know, actions taken, point of contact. Will wait for root cause confirmation before sending.
leah_sec: immediate risk classification: possible data exposure of non-sensitive path fragments and debug snippets. Unknown whether auth tokens leaked. Escalating to legal/comms if we confirm object exposure containing secrets.
samir_oncall: rotation in progress — rotated IAM role `logshipper-upload-role` and issued new trust policy restricting to internal endpoints only. New role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/logshipper-upload-role (rotated).
incident-bot: NOTE — rotation executed by samir_oncall at 3151600002. Audit link: https://playbook.internal/audit/rotate/3151600002
matt_prod: deploying patched forwarder (removing debug path metadata) to staging. Will push canary for 5 hosts then roll.
jenna_sre: forensics: I found two objects uploaded to `s3://external-relay-uploads/` from our forwarder IPs. Copying them to forensics bucket and preserving metadata.
leah_sec: do not publicly share object contents. Forensically imaging and scanning for credentials now.
olivia_cs: if customers affected, suggest offering a private channel with assigned CS lead + security contact.
samir_oncall: handing off live mitigation to leah_sec and jenna_sre for deeper analysis. I’ll stay available for infra changes.
leah_sec: taking lead for triage and remediation. Next steps: 1) complete forensic scan 2) determine exposure scope 3) prepare customer-impact assessment 4) prepare external notification checklist if required.
incident-bot: ACTION SUMMARY (automated): mitigations executed: connector disabled, svc-logshipper sessions revoked, upload role rotated, suspect objects preserved. Next owner: leah_sec. Link to incident doc draft: https://incidents.internal/3151599999
samir_oncall: thanks all. If leah needs emergency infra help ping me directly.
leah_sec: will update thread with final scope and response plan. Starting a short postmortem draft after containment.
olivia_cs: copied — will hold off on customer comms until sec gives go.
jenna_sre: logging note: create follow-up Jira `INF-4321` for permanent fix to forwarder metadata leak and add stricter allowlist enforcement.
leah_sec: tagging legal and comms: @legal-team @comms — please standby.
incident-bot: closing note: incident moved from P1 -> containment (P2) at 3151601399. For follow-up, runbook link: https://playbook.internal/runbooks/logshipper-leak
